signature.name: Alexander Nevsky Cathedral, Sofia
signature.detail: This gold-domed cathedral is Sofia's most recognizable symbol and a masterpiece of Balkan Orthodox architecture. Go early in the morning to avoid crowds and see the interior frescoes in quiet light; entry to the crypt museum is separate and modestly priced.

signature.name: Boyana Church
signature.detail: A UNESCO World Heritage site famous for its 13th-century frescoes, considered precursors of the Renaissance. Visits are limited to 10 minutes inside to protect the art, so book a timed slot in advance and take bus 64 from the city center.

signature.name: Church of St George (Rotunda)
signature.detail: A 4th-century Roman rotunda church tucked in a courtyard behind the Sheraton, with layers of medieval frescoes. It's free to enter and open daily; dress respectfully and avoid services.

signature.name: Vitosha Boulevard
signature.detail: Sofia's main pedestrian artery, lined with shops, cafes and views of Vitosha Mountain. It's best at sunset when locals stroll; start from the Palace of Justice and walk toward the mountain.
